blocks.text: Stoichiometry comes from the Greek words stoicheion, element, and metron, measure: the quantitative measure of reactants and products. It is the branch of chemistry in which the relationship between the amounts of reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation is studied. A balanced equation has the same number of atoms of each type on both sides and definite ratios of reactants and products, just as compounds have definite ratios of elements, and these ratios are used to calculate the mass or moles of other substances. Stoichiometric calculations obey the law of conservation of mass, which says that matter (mass) can neither be created nor destroyed, so the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a balanced equation, and the law of definite proportions, by which a pure compound always contains the same elements combined in the same ratio by mass.

blocks.title: Mole
blocks.text: The mole is the amount of a substance which contains as many elementary entities as there are atoms in 0.012 kg (12 g) of carbon-12. The entities may be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons or other particles. It is represented by n.

The number of entities in one mole of a substance is a constant called Avogadro's number, 6.02 x 10^23, represented by NA and attributed to the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro (1776-1856). Its exact value is 6.02214179 x 10^23 per mol; in calculations the rounded value 6.02 x 10^23 is used. One mole of carbon-12 contains 6.02 x 10^23 atoms, one mole of H2O 6.02 x 10^23 molecules, one mole of NaCl 6.02 x 10^23 formula units, and one mole of Na+ 6.02 x 10^23 ions. Chemists use the mole as the SI unit to weigh and count atoms, molecules, formula units or ions.

blocks.title: Molar mass
blocks.text: The mass of one mole of a substance (element, compound or ionic species), equal to its atomic, molecular, formula or ionic mass expressed in grams, is its molar mass, M, in g/mol. It is the sum of the masses of the component atoms.

The molar mass of CCl4 is the molar mass of one carbon plus four chlorines: 12.0 x 1 + 35.5 x 4 = 12.0 + 142.0 = 154.0 g. One mole of carbon atoms is 12.0 g, one mole of CO2 molecules 44.0 g, one mole of CaO formula units 56.1 g and one mole of carbonate ions 60.0 g. The number of moles is the given mass divided by the molar mass: n = m / M.

blocks.prompt: Calculate the molar mass of KMnO4, the moles in 0.23 g of sodium, the mass of 1.5 mol of Ca(OH)2, the moles in 24.5 g of KClO3, and the atoms in a 15 g gold ring (Au = 197).

items: Stoichiometry (stoicheion, metron) measures reactants and products from a balanced equation, obeying the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions.

A mole holds as many entities as atoms in 12 g of carbon-12: Avogadro's number, 6.02 x 10^23 (NA). Molar mass M (g/mol) is the atomic, molecular, formula or ionic mass in grams (CCl4 154.0); n = m / M.
